unit.title: Authentication Boundary: Engineer a Local Credential Verifier
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student building practical software-engineering habits
prerequisite_assumptions: ability to run Python unittest from a terminal
learning_objectives: Turn an authentication threat model into explicit component requirements and trust boundaries
Implement a small defensive credential-verification component using standard-library cryptographic primitives rather than custom cryptography
Define failure behavior, state invariants, and a test seam before treating the component as complete
Use deterministic unit tests to examine success, failure, malformed state, and nondeterministic inputs
Explain the gap between an educational component and a production authentication service

included: a local, in-memory password credential store
one-way verifier storage with per-record salts
threat modeling, unit testing, and an engineering note
excluded: network services or testing against live systems
account recovery, sessions, authorization, MFA, rate limiting, and distributed storage
official MIT lectures, notes, recordings, or lab specifications that were not retrieved
a claim of completing the authentication module or the course

completion_policy.decision_authority: Only a validator controlled by the learning-factory worker harness may mark this unit complete.
unit_completion_requires: all listed learner deliverables are present
the submitted test suite passes in the assigned environment
independent checks confirm the required authentication behavior and storage invariants
the threat model and engineering note are consistent with the implementation
the comprehension responses demonstrate reasoning about the learner's own artifact
completion_policy.course_completion_rule: This kickoff cannot establish completion of an MIT module, the six described labs, or the approximately 50-hour course. Later units require separately retrieved, classified, prepared, and validated evidence.
